report.summary: Reviewed chunk 8 of render.py; contains helper functions for HTML rendering of map counts, legends, entry table, module table and an absent-section fallback.
risks: absent_section | medium | The 'why' message references hand-written maps and no scanner derivation; this is a design assumption that may confuse users if the system changes. | Check that the message is still accurate for the current workflow.

_counts_bar | low | The hardcoded order of cells and the comment about 'island + orphan + unknown + shim' being exactly 'gate_unreached' is an assumption that could break if counts dict changes. | Verify that gate_unreached always equals sum of those four categories.
_entry_table | low | Uses 'ENTRY_KINDS' imported from reach module; if that list changes, the table may miss or misorder kinds. | Ensure ENTRY_KINDS is kept in sync with the data.

_module_table | low | Hardcoded order tuple and open_attr logic depend on specific class names; if CLASSES changes, the fallback ordering may produce unexpected results. | Keep the order tuple aligned with CLASSES.

handoff.purpose: Helper functions for generating HTML for absent sections, counts bar, legends, entry table, and module table.

symbols.name: absent_section
symbols.note: Returns HTML for a missing section with a reason why it's absent.

symbols.name: _counts_bar
symbols.note: Generates HTML divs for a counts bar showing various module counts.

symbols.name: _legend
symbols.note: Generates HTML for the status legend using STATUS_VOCAB.

symbols.name: _class_legend
symbols.note: Generates HTML for the class legend using CLASSES, CLASS_STATUS, and CLASS_MEANING.

symbols.name: _entry_table
symbols.note: Generates HTML table of entry points grouped by kind.

symbols.name: _module_table
symbols.note: Generates HTML table of modules grouped by classification.

claims.why: The code constructs this exact string in the else branch.

claims.text: This half of the map is hand-written on purpose: no scanner derives it, so nothing was generated in its place.
claims.why: The string appears verbatim in the returned HTML.

claims.text: island + orphan + unknown + shim, and the tiles beside it add up to exactly this.
claims.why: The comment claims that gate_unreached equals sum of those four categories, but the code only outputs gate_unreached as a single number; the sum is not computed or verified in this chunk.

claims.text: The alarms open by default; "reachable" and "test" are the long tail and stay folded
claims.why: The code sets open_attr for classes in ('island','orphan','unknown','shim') and not for others, matching the claim.

observations.what: absent_section returns HTML with a hardcoded message about hand-written maps; the function is used when a narrative section is missing.
_counts_bar builds a list of cells with hardcoded status classes and labels; the order is fixed and includes 'gate_unreached' as a summary.
_legend and _class_legend both use external constants (STATUS_VOCAB, CLASSES, CLASS_STATUS, CLASS_MEANING) that are not defined in this chunk.
_entry_table imports ENTRY_KINDS from .reach; the table groups entries by kind and shows name, module, function, and targets.
_module_table imports CLASSES from .reach; it orders classes with a hardcoded tuple and opens details for certain classes by default.
